newsitem.title: UK: PRESS DIGEST - FINANCIAL TIMES JUNE 4.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - FINANCIAL TIMES JUNE 4.

text.p: PRESS DIGEST - Financial Times - This daily press summary is produced for Reuters by the Broadcast Monitoring Company, which is responsible for its contents. For further information on these articles or details of BMC's other international press and broadcast services call Simon McMillan on +44 (0)171 256 5130 or e-mail bmc.co@ft.com
-- PRUDENTIAL ORDERED TO RE-TEST ITS ENTIRE SALES STAFF

The London City watchdog has ordered pensions and insurance group Prudential to re-test its entire sales staff after a SIB report into the company revealed that the group advised some of its non-taxpaying clients to buy one of its products when those of other companies would have been more suitable. Over 5,500 sales personnel will be re-tested in training and compliance procedures this summer.
-- OFWAT ATTACKS WATER GROUPS' PAYOUTS

The UK's water industry regulator, Ian Byatt, has lashed out against substantial increases in dividend payments to shareholders of water and sewerage companies, calling them 'unsustainable' and politically dangerous. Byatt warned that increases were sending wrong messages to the public during a period when the government is emphasising windfall taxes on privatised utilities adding that water investors need no better returns than others.
-- BECKETT TO LEAVE TAKEOVER RULES UNCHANGED

On Wednesday, it is expected that the UK's trade and industry secretary, Margaret Beckett, will drop the long-standing government proposal to increase the difficulty of takeovers through forcing companies to show they are in the public's interest. Beckett will also terminate all plans to merge the Office of Fair Trading with the Monopolies and Mergers Commission.
-- EU RAISES DOUBTS ON DIGITAL TV LICENCE BID

European competition commissioner Karel van Miert has expressed concerns over Digital Broadcasting's bid to offer digital terrestrial services in the UK. Van Meirt suggested that problems may arise with the same operator dominating conventional broadcasting, satellite broadcasting as well as the digital sector.
-- RACAL ISSUES THIRD PROFIT WARNING

Speculation is growing among analysts that defence electronics group Racal may be broken up after the company announced its third profits warning in six months and said it was appointing advisers to assist on long-term decisions on its data products business and the telecoms network services. Announcing a 43 per cent fall in group pre-tax profits, to 40.4 million stg, chairman Sir Ernest Harrison denied that the group was 'for sale'.
-- COCA COLA TRIES TO OUST RIVAL AT MCDONALD'S

Soft drinks giant Coca Cola has launched an initiative aimed at pushing rival Cadbury Schweppes out of thousands of McDonald's fast-food outlets in the US. Coca Cola has offered 'conversion allowances' to McDonald's franchisees of between 200 and 600 gallons of free soft drink syrup if they agree to exclusively serve Coca Cola products in their restaurants.
-- EUROPEAN TELECOMS PARTNERS TO TIGHTEN LINKS

European telecoms alliance Unisource, which includes KPN of the Netherlands, Telia of Sweden and the Swiss national operator, has moved to strengthen ties between its members following the defection last month of Spain's Telefonica. The three remaining partners have said they intend to merge their carrier services operations into a $2 billion (1.2 billion stg)
turnover pan- European carrier.
-- RECORD YEAR FOR VODAFONE

Vodafone, the UK's largest mobile phone operator, has reported annual pre-tax profits up 13 per cent at 539 million stg. Revenues at the group were ahead 25 percent at 1.75 billion stg. Vodafone's international operations moved into the black for the first time, contributing 10.5 million stg to group pre-tax profits. Announcing the results, chief executive Chris Gent said the group had achieved good subscriber growth in the US and extended its lead in digital services.
-- DAIRY CREST ATTACKS SUPPLIER

UK milk buyer Dairy Crest has launched an attack on Milk Marque, the sellers' co-operative, for seeking to process its surplus milk into butter and skimmed milk powder. The criticism came as Dairy Crest reported a 13 per cent rise in pre-tax profits after exceptionals in its first full year results since floatation last year. Dairy Crest also called on Milk Marque to cut its prices.
-- NATIONAL GRID SIGNALS CHANGE OF POLICY ON ENERGIS

Electricity transmission group National Grid has indicated that it intends to hold on - at least in the medium term - to Energis, its telecommunications company. National Grid had previously planned to sell a large stake in Energis, but group chief executive David Jones said Tuesday that the subsidiary had developed successfully in the past year through a series of commercial business arrangements with other telecommunications companies.
